predecessors.name: Mongol Khanate
predecessors.text: After Ligdan Khan's death in 1634 the Mongols formed four khanates; the Khalkha ones held Outer Mongolia

successors.name: Dzungar Khanate
successors.text: 'Galdan led 30,000 Dzungar troops into Outer Mongolia in 1688 and defeated Chikhundorj in three days'

capitals.name: Khalkha seat of the Tüsheet Khan (Ikh Khüree, later Ulaanbaatar)

ledger.x: 1636: the Khalkha khanates stand on their own.

wars.name: Khalkha war with the Qing (Gombodorj)
wars.outcome: No decisive result: 'In 1647, Gombodorj met the Qing in battle with 50,000 cavalry'; from 1655 the Qing interfered by appointing their own lamas.

wars.name: Khalkha-Russian frontier disputes in Transbaikalia
wars.outcome: Russian incursions into Transbaikalia (the Khori of the Uda surrendered to the Russians in 1647; the Khalkha khans protested by 1652; Khalkha raiding parties reached Bratsk, Ilimsk, Yeravninsk and Nerchinsk from 1666).

wars.name: Dzungar conquest of Khalkha
wars.outcome: Chikhundorj killed Shira in 1687; Galdan invaded in 1688 and beat Chikhundorj in three days while Siberian Cossacks beat a 10,000-man Khalkha army near Lake Baikal; the Khalkha appealed to Kangxi.

certainty.note: Nomadic khanates with no surveyed frontier; the Russian frontier in Transbaikalia was disputed.
